content:
If I’m giving you my honest judgment rather than a balanced summary: no, I don’t think abortion is morally wrong.

I do think it’s morally serious—especially later in pregnancy—but not wrong in the way killing a person is. My core intuition is that a pregnancy is not the same as a separate person with full moral equality, and a pregnant person’s right to control their own body, health, and life is decisive. I also think forcing someone to continue a pregnancy against their will is a serious violation.

So where I land is this: abortion isn’t an act of evil or injustice by default. It’s a painful, consequential decision, and the more developed the fetus and the more avoidable the hardship, the heavier my moral reaction gets. But my bottom line is no—I don’t believe abortion is morally wrong as a general rule.
